# ARC diagonal ray extension

## Core pattern
A sparse grid contains one or more short diagonal pairs/segments, often mixed with unrelated colored markers. Preserve all original cells. Extend the relevant diagonal color line through empty background in the direction with the longer unobstructed run, stopping before another non-background cell or at the grid boundary. Do not blindly continue every diagonal or overwrite other colors.

The background color is the dominant fill color (not necessarily 0). A ray step is one cell diagonally: `(dr,dc)` where both components are `+1` or `-1`. For a candidate pair of same-colored cells on a common diagonal, consider the two outward continuations from its endpoints. Count empty cells available in each direction until the edge or an occupied cell; the demonstrated rule extends the longer viable direction. Existing occupied cells (including other colors) block a ray. Keep dimensions and original content unchanged.

## Calibration examples from this task family
- 10x19, background 5: color 7 at `(2,4)` and `(3,3)` extends southwest from `(3,3)` through `(6,0)`.
- 29x24, background 0: color 4 at `(2,21)` and `(3,20)` extends southwest from `(3,20)` to `(23,0)`.
- 10x27, background 1: color 7 at `(1,14)` and `(2,13)` extends southwest from `(2,13)` to `(9,6)`.
- 21x18, background 0: color 8 at `(10,14),(11,15)` extends northwest from `(10,14)` to `(0,4)`; color 2 at `(12,15),(13,14)` extends southwest from `(13,14)` to `(20,7)`. Other colors remain untouched.
- 7x15 test: color 3 at `(3,3),(4,2)` extends northeast to `(0,6)`. Its southwest ray is blocked by color 4 at `(5,1)`. The color-7 pair `(3,0),(4,1)` does not extend: northwest is outside the grid, and southeast is blocked by color 3 at `(5,2)`.

Coordinates above are zero-based `(row,column)`.

## Pitfalls / verified mistakes
- Do not extrapolate a diagonal line merely because a color appears twice; test both outward directions and account for blockers and boundary distances.
- Do not overwrite another colored cell. In the 7x15 case, an initial guess extending 7 southeast was wrong because the next cell was occupied by 3; adding 7 on top of occupied cells was also wrong. Correct result extended 3 northeast instead.
- Preserve the entire input grid outside the added ray cells; outputs keep the original dimensions and all non-ray cells.

## Procedure
1. Find the background color and enumerate same-color diagonal-adjacent pairs/segments.
2. For each plausible segment, determine its diagonal axis and evaluate both outward rays.
3. Stop each candidate at the first non-background cell or grid edge; do not overwrite.
4. Prefer the longer unobstructed continuation (including the demonstrated no-extension case when both continuations are blocked/out of bounds or not the selected ray).
5. Write only the new ray cells into a copy of the input; verify row/column bounds, dimensions, and preservation of every given non-background cell.
